name: Oracle-free extraction metrics (recall, compression, round-trip fixed point) -- a synthesis across several distinct methodologies rather than one paper: WCXB's supplementary snippet-recall/boilerplate-rate figures, MINEA (Multiple Infused Needle Extraction Accuracy), SUSWIR (compression-ratio + semantic-similarity summary scoring without reference), Round-Trip Correctness (RTC, Allamanis et al., ICML 2024, arXiv:2402.08699) applied by analogy from code to extraction, and 'Beyond a Single Extractor' (arXiv:2602.19548)'s downstream-task proxy evaluation.
kind: A cluster of evaluation methodologies (research results), not a single tool, standard or benchmark -- grouped here because the project's own interest (fields.yaml's `roundtrip_safety` and `independent_oracle` fields) is in the METHOD of ground-truth-free evaluation, not any one paper's numbers.
maturity: Mixed. RTC is the most mature and directly transferable (ICML 2024, peer-reviewed, Pearson r=0.95-0.96 validated against supervised pass@1/pass@k on two benchmarks). MINEA and SUSWIR are newer, narrower research proposals for information-extraction/summarization quality, not web-content extraction specifically. WCXB's snippet-recall/boilerplate-rate pair is a SUPPLEMENTARY metric inside a reference-based benchmark, not a standalone oracle-free method, but it approximates one because 'required snippets' and 'boilerplate admitted' can be computed with a much lighter-weight reference than full span-level ground truth. 'Beyond a Single Extractor' is a 2026 preprint proposing downstream-task performance as the proxy, an established but indirect idea (already standard in the LLM-pretraining-data literature).
license: Not applicable in the conventional sense -- these are methodologies/papers, not licensed software. Where implementations exist (WCXB's scoring scripts, RTC's reference code), they inherit each paper's own release terms, not independently confirmed here for RTC/MINEA/SUSWIR.
keeps_and_discards: Each method targets a different failure surface. Snippet recall (WCXB) keeps a lightweight PARTIAL reference (a curated list of must-have text snippets per page rather than a full span) and discards everything about ordering/formatting -- cheaper to construct than full ground truth but still reference-based, so only 'oracle-LIGHT' not fully oracle-free. MINEA discards the need for any pre-existing labeled corpus by injecting synthetic 'needle' entities (occupying 10-30% of the enriched document) whose presence/absence is trivially checkable -- but it only tests RECALL of known-inserted content, not precision against organic boilerplate. SUSWIR discards reference text entirely, scoring extraction via semantic-similarity-to-source + METEOR-style relevance + redundancy-avoidance, but the paper's own limitation is that it is COMPARATIVE (ranks extractions against each other) not absolute, and 'cannot definitively measure if entities are missing, misclassified, or their properties not filled in correctly.' RTC discards reference text by using a forward/backward model PAIR and checking round-trip fixed-point recovery, at the cost of coupling two model capabilities together.
structure_preserved: Not a property of the metrics themselves; each measures a different notion of fidelity: snippet recall/boilerplate rate operates on text content, not structure; MINEA operates on entity presence; SUSWIR operates on semantic content overlap; RTC in its original code-domain form checks functional/structural equivalence of REGENERATED code, which is a stronger structural check than any of the pure-text extraction metrics -- an analogous 'regenerate-then-diff-structure' RTC variant for HTML->markdown->HTML would need to be defined for this project, and none of the surveyed sources does so.
interactive_elements: Not addressed by any of the five methods -- all target text-content extraction quality, not interactive-control fidelity.
interactive_state_fidelity: Not addressed -- no surveyed oracle-free method has any notion of control state (checked/disabled/expanded).
layout_awareness: None of the five methods reads or requires rendered layout; all operate on extracted text or DOM/HTML source.
javascript_required: Not inherent to any of the metrics -- they are scoring functions applied AFTER extraction, agnostic to whether the extractor itself executed JavaScript. WCXB's own corpus (source of the snippet-recall figures) is static-HTML-only (see the WCXB item), so its snippet-recall numbers do not reflect JS-rendered pages.
evaluation_method: Five distinct oracle-free-adjacent strategies: (1) WCXB SNIPPET RECALL/BOILERPLATE RATE -- percentage of curated required snippets found in extractor output (recall) vs. percentage of extractor output that is non-required text (boilerplate admitted), a lighter-weight reference than full ground truth but still reference-based; (2) MINEA -- synthetic needle-entity injection into real documents at known locations, then measuring extraction recall of the inserted needles, generating ground truth ON THE FLY rather than by human annotation; (3) SUSWIR -- reference-free by construction, combining semantic-similarity-to-source-document, METEOR-based relevance, and self-referenced redundancy into one convex score, no gold summary/extraction needed at all; (4) ROUND-TRIP CORRECTNESS (RTC) -- forward model M (e.g. extract-to-markdown) composed with a backward model M^-1 (markdown-to-reconstructed-page or markdown-to-description), checking whether x_hat = M^-1(M(x)) is semantically/functionally equivalent to x, with NO human reference required if a good similarity/equivalence oracle exists; (5) DOWNSTREAM-TASK PROXY (Beyond a Single Extractor) -- train/evaluate a model on extractor output and measure standard-benchmark performance (Core_V2, MMLU, WikiTableQuestions, HumanEval) as an indirect quality signal, explicitly because the paper found 'these metrics don't always predict how well LLMs can be trained on extractor outputs' when human-extraction reference metrics were used instead.
corpus_size_and_origins: WCXB snippet-recall figures: computed over the same 2,008-page/1,613-domain WCXB test corpus (see that item) -- rs-trafilatura 75.6% required-snippet recall at 9.6% boilerplate admitted; Resiliparse 74.5% snippet recall at 22.8% boilerplate admitted (substantially more boilerplate for similar recall); Trafilatura 69.5% snippet recall. MINEA/SUSWIR corpus sizes not confirmed from available sources (general information-extraction/summarization test sets, not web-specific). RTC's original validation: HumanEval and ARCADE code benchmarks (not web content). 'Beyond a Single Extractor' evaluates on an unspecified large-scale web-crawl pretraining corpus with a finding that only 39% of pages survive as overlapping extractions across multiple extractors tested -- exact page/domain counts not confirmed from the fetched excerpt.
reported_precision_recall: WCXB snippet recall/boilerplate pair (denominator = curated required-snippet list per page, over the WCXB test corpus): rs-trafilatura 75.6% recall / 9.6% boilerplate; Resiliparse 74.5% recall / 22.8% boilerplate; Trafilatura 69.5% recall / 6.6% boilerplate (i.e. Trafilatura trades recall for cleanliness, Resiliparse trades cleanliness for recall -- a precision/recall tradeoff visible ONLY because the paper reports both, not just F1). RTC: Pearson r=0.95, Spearman rho=0.90 correlation with HumanEval pass@1-style scores; same r=0.95/rho=0.90 on ARCADE -- i.e. RTC as an unsupervised proxy tracks supervised code-correctness metrics almost as well as the supervised metrics track each other. MINEA/SUSWIR: no directly comparable extraction-domain precision/recall figures confirmed from available sources.
independent_oracle: This field IS the subject of the item. Ranked by how independent the check is from the thing being checked: MINEA is the most genuinely independent (the needle's ground-truth existence is asserted by the test harness at injection time, not derived from any model output) but only tests recall of INSERTED content, not real extraction quality on organic boilerplate. RTC is independent in the sense that no human labels the round-trip target, but is NOT independent of the forward/backward MODEL PAIR's shared biases -- the paper's own stated failure mode (adversarial vulnerability: forward model memorizes input, backward model copies it, perfect RTC score without genuine capability) is exactly a case where the 'oracle' collapses into a tautology. SUSWIR is reference-free but self-admittedly comparative rather than absolute -- it cannot serve as a true oracle, only a ranking signal. WCXB's snippet recall is NOT oracle-free at all -- it substitutes a cheaper partial reference for a full one, still human-curated.
evidence_independence: WCXB's snippet-recall figures come from the same independent (non-vendor) research group as its main F1 evaluation (see that item). RTC's validation is academic (Microsoft Research-adjacent authorship per typical ICML publication pattern; not independently reconfirmed here) and cross-validated against two separate supervised benchmarks (HumanEval, ARCADE), which is a meaningfully strong independence signal for the METHOD even though it was validated in the code domain, not web extraction. MINEA and SUSWIR: academic, not vendor-produced, per available sources, but neither has been independently re-validated by a second research group in the sources found here.
page_archetype_coverage: Only WCXB's snippet-recall figures inherit archetype coverage (via the same 7-type corpus as WCXB's F1 table), though the recall/boilerplate breakdown BY archetype was not separately confirmed in this pass (only aggregate figures were found). None of MINEA, SUSWIR, RTC, or the downstream-proxy method has any page-archetype dimension -- all are archetype-agnostic by design, which is itself a gap if this project adopts one of them: a needle-injection or round-trip check calibrated only on article-shaped pages could silently fail on forum/product-shaped pages the same way WCXB found heuristic extractors do.
script_and_locale_behaviour: Not addressed by any of the five methods in available sources. MINEA's needle-generation presumably depends on an LLM capable of the target language/script; RTC's forward/backward model pair likewise inherits whatever script/language competence the chosen models have. None reports a script-invariance test.
leaks_outward: Not applicable -- these are offline scoring methodologies, not live capture mechanisms.
countermeasures: Not applicable in the privacy sense.
measured_fidelity_cost: Not applicable in the privacy-hardening sense, though RTC's own literature explicitly measures a DIFFERENT fidelity cost: the gap between RTC score and true supervised-metric score when the forward model produces implausible samples ('if the forward model produces implausible samples, measuring the backward model's true capability becomes impossible') -- i.e. RTC has a documented, honestly-reported cost/failure mode rather than an unstated one.
gate_state_at_capture: Not applicable -- none of the five methods concerns live page capture.
determinism: WCXB's snippet-recall scoring is deterministic (fixed corpus, fixed required-snippet lists). RTC is only as deterministic as its forward/backward models -- if run with a temperature>0 LLM as either M or M^-1, RTC scores would vary run-to-run, a property the RTC paper does not appear to fully quantify in the excerpts fetched here. MINEA's needle generation, if LLM-driven, has the same non-determinism risk unless needles are cached/fixed after generation.
determinism_across_versions: Not addressed by any source for any of the five methods -- an open gap across this entire methodological literature, consistent with the same gap found in WCXB and the CleanEval-lineage benchmarks.
reproducibility: RTC is the most reproducible in principle since it repurposes EXISTING project artifacts (e.g. unit tests already in a codebase) rather than requiring new annotation -- for a web-extraction analogue this could mean using a page's OWN existing structured data (schema.org markup, OpenGraph tags) as the round-trip check, an idea not stated in the RTC paper but a natural extension. MINEA's synthetic-ground-truth generation is reproducible by construction (the injected needles are known exactly at generation time) but depends on stable needle-generation prompts if LLM-driven. SUSWIR and the downstream-task-proxy method depend on stable underlying models/benchmarks (MMLU, Core_V2 etc.) for reproducibility, which are themselves subject to benchmark contamination/versioning concerns not explored in the source material.
failure_modes: RTC's paper documents three explicit failure modes worth importing verbatim into this project's own thinking: (1) similarity-function dependency -- a weak semantic-equivalence check makes RTC meaningless regardless of the forward/backward models' quality; (2) coupled-task interdependence -- a bad forward model corrupts the ability to measure the backward model, and vice versa, so a single RTC number cannot localize WHICH direction failed; (3) adversarial/degenerate collapse -- memorize-and-copy achieves a perfect score without demonstrating real capability, explicitly flagged as 'unlikely under common training' but real under optimization pressure. SUSWIR's failure mode is that it is comparative, not absolute, so a whole-corpus SUSWIR improvement could still hide per-page catastrophic misses. MINEA's failure mode is that a system could pass on synthetic needles (which look statistically unusual/salient) while failing on real, stylistically-blended boilerplate/content boundaries -- the needle is, in effect, an out-of-distribution probe.
failure_visibility: RTC and MINEA both fail LOUDLY in the sense that their scores are directly interpretable numbers with known failure semantics (documented in the RTC paper's limitations section) -- this is a stronger property than most vendor-run HTML-to-markdown comparisons in this research set, which rarely discuss their own failure modes at all.
scale_limits: Not addressed by any source in a scale-of-corpus sense. RTC's COST scales with running two models (forward + backward) per evaluated item rather than one, roughly doubling inference cost versus a single-pass reference-based check -- an implicit but unstated tradeoff.
delta_cost_model: Not applicable -- none of these methods has an incremental-update notion; each scores a document (or document pair) as a whole.
reanchoring_stability: Not applicable directly, though MINEA's needle-injection technique is structurally similar in spirit to content-addressing/re-anchoring tests this project already uses elsewhere (inserting a known marker and checking whether it survives a transformation) -- the analogy is worth noting even though MINEA's own domain is entity extraction, not DOM re-anchoring.
adversarial_exposure: Directly relevant: RTC's documented adversarial-collapse failure mode (forward model memorizes, backward model copies, perfect score with no real signal) is exactly the kind of gaming risk this project's `adversarial_exposure` field should track if a round-trip fixed-point check is adopted as a fidelity metric -- an attacker or a degenerate pipeline could satisfy 'serialize->parse->serialize is a fixed point' trivially by never transforming content at all, which would score PERFECTLY on roundtrip_safety while providing zero extraction value. This is the single most load-bearing risk surfaced by this item for the project's own design.
provenance_carrying: Not addressed by any of the five methods -- none carries or checks per-token provenance as part of its scoring.
roundtrip_safety: This field is essentially synonymous with the RTC methodology itself: RTC IS the formalization of 'serialize -> parse -> serialize is a fixed point' as an evaluation metric, generalized from code (describe<->generate) to any domain with a plausible forward/backward model pair. Its transferability risk to web-content extraction specifically is that HTML->markdown->HTML is inherently LOSSY by design (markdown cannot represent all HTML), so a naive round-trip check would either (a) never reach a true fixed point, requiring a semantic-equivalence oracle rather than exact-match, or (b) need to be defined at the markdown->concept-tree->markdown level (matching this project's own architecture) rather than markdown->HTML->markdown, which the RTC literature does not address for this specific domain.
token_budget_and_ordering: Not addressed by any of the five methods -- none has a token-budget or context-ordering dimension; all evaluate whole-document fidelity, not truncation-aware fidelity.
representation_cost: The downstream-task-proxy method (Beyond a Single Extractor) is the one source in this cluster that DOES engage representation cost, via its 'token yield' metric -- e.g. combining multiple extractors increased token yield by up to 71% while maintaining benchmark performance, treating token yield as an efficiency proxy rather than a quality metric per se, and explicitly noting only 39% of pages survive as overlapping extractions across multiple extractors, meaning single-extractor evaluation systematically under-samples what a multi-extractor or extractor-agnostic (structure-agnostic) approach could capture.
what_could_be_adopted: Two mechanisms are directly adoptable, one is adoptable-with-modification, one is a negative lesson. ADOPTABLE: (1) WCXB's recall/boilerplate-rate PAIR (rather than a single F1) as a lightweight, cheaper-than-full-ground-truth oracle-light check for this project's own dedup/extraction fold -- a small curated required-snippet list per test page is far cheaper to build than full span ground truth and still yields two independently interpretable numbers. (2) MINEA-style synthetic needle injection as a genuinely oracle-free recall check for THIS project's own pipeline: inject a known, uniquely-identifiable marker string into a real page's DOM before ingest, then verify it survives capture/dedup/serialization -- this requires no human annotation and directly tests the pipeline's own no-mocks, real-browser path. ADOPTABLE WITH MODIFICATION: RTC-style round-trip fixed-point checking, but only if defined at the markdown<->concept-tree level (matching this project's actual architecture) with an explicit safeguard against the degenerate-collapse failure mode (e.g. the round-trip target must differ nontrivially from a null transform, verified by injecting a known DELTA between the two directions rather than checking pure identity). NEGATIVE LESSON: SUSWIR's own admission that reference-free compression/similarity scores are comparative, not absolute, means this project should never report a bare oracle-free score as if it were ground-truth-equivalent precision/recall -- it should always be paired with the MINEA-style synthetic-needle absolute check for at least a subset of measurements.
constraint_violation_ledger: structure_agnosticism: ADOPTABLE AS-IS for all five methods -- none requires naming a region nav/article/result; MINEA injects entities without regard to page region, RTC operates on whole-document transforms, SUSWIR/snippet-recall operate on text content without structural classification. no_layout_in_the_fold: ADOPTABLE AS-IS -- none of the five reads geometry. o_delta: NOT APPLICABLE for four of the five (whole-document, one-shot scoring); MINEA-style needle injection COULD be adapted into an O(delta) check by injecting/removing a needle and measuring whether only the affected subtree's re-ingest cost changes, which would double as an oracle-free O(delta) falsifiability test -- this is a novel extension not present in the source literature but directly implied by combining MINEA with the project's own delta_cost_model field. no_mocks: ADOPTABLE AS-IS AS A PRINCIPLE, WITH ONE NAMED RISK -- RTC's own degenerate-collapse failure mode is structurally a 'mock' in disguise (a forward/backward pair that colludes to fake fidelity without doing real work), so adopting round-trip checking without RTC's own documented safeguards would silently violate the spirit of no_mocks even while satisfying its letter. closed_shadow_roots_stay_closed: NOT APPLICABLE -- none of the five methods concerns shadow-DOM capture; a needle could in principle be placed inside a closed shadow root specifically to test whether the pipeline honestly reports it as unreachable rather than silently failing, which would be a useful project-specific extension. OVERALL VERDICT: adoptable as-is at the METHODOLOGY level (snippet-recall pairing and MINEA-style needle injection), adoptable in the actuator layer only for RTC-style round-trip checking (needs a project-specific equivalence oracle and an explicit anti-collapse safeguard), and the SUSWIR/downstream-proxy approaches are negative-oracle-only -- useful for relative ranking across pipeline changes, never as a claimed absolute fidelity number.
governance_signal_handling: Not addressed by any of the five methods -- orthogonal concern.
legal_basis_and_pii_posture: Not addressed by any of the five methods -- orthogonal concern, though MINEA-style needle injection into REAL captured pages (rather than synthetic test fixtures) would need the same PII/legal-basis review as any other real-page retention this project already applies, since the needle is inserted into an otherwise-real page's content stream.
uncertain: corpus_size_and_origins for MINEA and SUSWIR (their evaluation corpora were not confirmed from available sources -- both appear to be general information-extraction/summarization test sets, not web-content-specific, but exact sizes were not found)

reported_precision_recall for MINEA/SUSWIR in the web-extraction domain specifically (both papers' primary validation appears to be outside pure web-content extraction; numbers found were for RTC in the code domain and WCXB's snippet-recall pair, not for MINEA/SUSWIR directly)
determinism (whether RTC and MINEA's original papers use temperature=0/deterministic models in their published validation runs was not confirmed)

This item is inherently a synthesis across five separately-sourced methods rather than one paper with one coherent claim set -- several fields above represent reasoned extension/analogy (e.g. applying RTC's code-domain properties to web extraction) rather than a directly-cited result, and are flagged as such inline
